messages:
maria: Folks — quick follow-up from the heap postmortem. I sketched an owner + timeline list for remaining remediation work. Can volunteers confirm or reassign? :clipboard:
aj: happy to take the profiling run for the shard replicas. will post results by EOD tomorrow. :mag:
maria: thanks aj — can you also include GC pause histograms and a short reproducer script?
aj: yup. plan: reproduce with `wrk` load + `--kv-populate=100k`, then run `./profile-kv --heap --duration 10m` and upload flamegraphs.
sam: I'll own the soft-limit guardrail and metric alerts (RW-4821). ETA Thu COB.
leah: I can pair with sam on the alert thresholds. want to make sure we avoid churn from transient spikes. :thinking_face:
taylor: i will audit slab allocator knobs and try a small patch to cap slab growth. aiming for a canary by next week.
maria: high-level priorities: 1) repro + profiles (aj) 2) short-term guardrails/alerts (sam/leah) 3) GC/tuning + quantize slab (taylor) 4) retrospective doc + assignment handoff (me).
aj: quick question — for reproducer, is it OK to reuse the production dataset subset (anonymized) or do you want synthetic traffic?
maria: anonymized subset is fine as long as PII scrubbed. use stg-vpc and tag runs with `heap-whodunit` so CI artifacts attach.
ci-bot: Attached artifact: https://ci.internal/runs/2345 (heap profiles, 10m)
aj: uploaded initial flamegraph and trace: https://ci.internal/artifacts/2345/flame.svg — early signal: large residency from HTTP header parsing path, surprising.
sam: for alerts I'm thinking two tiers: soft limit at 70% heap residency (paged PSC) and hard alert at 90% + sustained >30s. Also add `oom_predicted` anomaly signal.
leah: that sounds reasonable. can we add a brief mute window (5m) after deploys to reduce noise?
maria: yes, let's add deploy windows. sam, can you create RW-4821 with that spec and link runbooks?
sam: created RW-4821: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RW-4821 — added owner leah as co-owner.
taylor: slab patch prototype pushed to fork: `taylor/limit-slab-growth`. bench results: 1.8% latency increase but memory drop ~12% under load.
aj: interesting — do you have trace showing fragment compaction rate change?
taylor: added `--emit-slab-metrics` to the canary, will share dashboards.
maria: for long-term: consider KV eviction heuristics and compact-on-insert paths. please add tickets if you find concrete work.
aj: adding RW-4827 for repro -> eviction experiments.
sam: i'll wire alert to not only page but also create an auto-rollover ticket with logs attached so on-call has context.
leah: one more ask: run a scheduled GC stress job nightly for a week and collect allocations by site. aj/taylor — can you coordinate?
aj: yes, i'll coordinate with taylor and schedule in workload-runner.
taylor: scheduled job `heap-sleuth-nightly` starting tonight at 02:15 UTC. it runs for 2 hours and uploads `alloc-sites.json`.
ci-bot: automated note: nightly job `heap-sleuth-nightly` created (run id 99877).
maria: awesome. I'll draft a short follow-up doc and include action table: owners, due dates, tickets. Expect a doc in #eng-runtime tomorrow morning.
sam: quick sanity check — do we want a temporary rate-limit on some upstream clients to ease pressure while we iterate?
leah: maybe throttle cheap ops (cold cache scans) — low risk. open a small config PR and we'll test in canary.
aj: logging note: increase KV alloc sampling rate to 1/100 for these experiments so we can see hotspots.
maria: agreed. final ask: everyone drop a 1-line update here when you complete your task so I can close the postmortem action list. :white_check_mark:
aj: will do.
sam: done — RW-4821 initial config pushed to staging (PR #389).
leah: PR for mute window and alert tweaks is out (#392).
taylor: canary deployed with slab cap, monitoring looks stable so far.
maria: thanks all — feel free to @me on any blockers. I'll sync this into the retro doc later today. :v:
